title: Quotas, TPM, RPM and 429s
summary: Providers limit tokens per minute and requests per minute. A 429 has more than one cause, and each provider counts tokens differently, so read the headers before you raise anything.
useIf: Requests fail with 429 while dashboards show spare quota, or many consumers share one deployment.
avoidIf: You plan to fix every 429 by asking for more quota or by retrying harder.

explain.md: On Azure, **quota** is a TPM allowance per subscription, region, model and deployment type. The TPM you assign becomes the deployment's limit, and **RPM** follows in proportion: 6 RPM per 1,000 TPM for older chat models and 1 RPM per 1,000 TPM for o3 and o4-mini [[r8]]. Responses carry `x-ratelimit-limit-requests`, `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens` and matching `reset` headers, and a 429 adds `retry-after-ms` [[r8]].

Azure documents several kinds of 429. Three to tell apart first are quota exceeded, system capacity throttling, and a temporary rate-limit adjustment on Standard deployments. Compare `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens` with your assigned TPM to spot the third [[r8]]. A fourth documented cause is a request whose `max_tokens` estimate inflates the counted tokens, so a 429 can appear below quota. The TPM check uses prompt tokens plus `max_tokens` plus `best_of`, so `max_tokens: 4000` reserves 4,000 tokens for a 200-token answer, and RPM is enforced over 1 or 10 second windows, so a 600 RPM deployment can throttle at more than 10 requests in one second [[r9]].

At scale, enforce **per-consumer limits at a gateway**: `llm-token-limit` limits by a `counter-key` in tokens per minute or as a quota per period, but its counts are estimates and are kept per gateway [[r2]]. When a 429 does arrive, honour `retry-after-ms` and never retry a quota-exhausted error.

explain.title: Reading a 429 (author synthesis)
explain.alt: A decision tree: if the limit header is below assigned TPM it is a temporary cut; if remaining headers are near zero it is quota or an RPM window; otherwise capacity throttling.

pitfalls.cause: Large `max_tokens` reserves tokens, or a burst exceeds the 1 to 10 second RPM window
pitfalls.fix: Set `max_tokens` near the real answer length and smooth bursts

pitfalls.cause: The 429 was capacity throttling or a temporary limit cut, not quota
pitfalls.fix: Read the headers, compare limit with assigned TPM, move traffic to another deployment or region

pitfalls.symptom: A retry loop turned a blip into an outage
pitfalls.cause: Quota-exhausted 429s were retried and each layer multiplied traffic
pitfalls.fix: Honour `retry-after-ms`, do not retry quota errors, count retries across SDK and app layers

scenarios.title: 429s with spare quota on the dashboard
scenarios.situation: An assistant answers in about 300 tokens but every call sets `max_tokens: 4000`. At peak, calls return 429 while the TPM graph reads 55% of quota.
unknowns: What do `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens` and the limit header say?
How many requests arrive in the busiest second?
Is there an overly wide `best_of` or `n`?
scenarios.question: What is the first fix?

options.name: Set `max_tokens` close to the real answer length and read the headers
options.why: Azure's TPM check counts prompt plus `max_tokens`, so each call reserves about 13 times what it uses. Right-sizing frees most of the allowance at no cost.
options.tradeoff: Answers longer than the cap are truncated, so measure the output length distribution first.

options.name: Request more quota
options.why: It treats a reservation artefact as a shortage and the request may be slow or denied.
options.tradeoff: Right when remaining-tokens headers sit near zero at sustained load.

options.name: Add client retries with backoff
options.why: Backoff with jitter smooths short bursts.
options.tradeoff: It does not reduce reservation waste and multiplies load if every layer retries.

flips.if: The limit header is lower than assigned TPM
flips.then: It is a temporary cut: route to a second deployment and wait.

flips.if: Bursts exceed the RPM window with ample TPM
flips.then: Smooth at a gateway queue or token bucket.

scenarios.takeaway: Oversized `max_tokens` is a quota tax. Right-size it before you ask for more.

scenarios.title: One team starves the others
scenarios.situation: Five teams share one Azure deployment. A new batch-style job from one team consumes most of the TPM at midday, and interactive teams see 429s.
unknowns: Can the batch job move to a Batch tier?
Do teams need monthly token quotas for chargeback?
scenarios.question: How do you protect interactive users?

options.name: Per-team `llm-token-limit` at the gateway, and move the batch job to Batch
options.why: Limits give each team a fair share with a 429 on rate and 403 on quota, and the Batch tier has its own enqueued-token quota.
options.tradeoff: Gateway estimates tokens and can briefly overshoot; counters are per gateway.

options.name: A separate deployment per team
options.tradeoff: Fragments quota so each team needs headroom for its own peaks.

options.name: Ask every team to retry more patiently
options.why: Retries add load while the noisy job keeps the quota exhausted.
options.tradeoff: Backoff is right for transient blips, not for a sustained shortfall.

flips.if: The gateway runs in several regions
flips.then: Counters are not aggregated, so split the limit per region or use a shared store.
Two deployments may be simpler than a gateway.

scenarios.takeaway: Shared quota needs per-consumer limits, or the loudest consumer wins.

quiz.q: A call has a 600-token prompt, `max_tokens: 4000` and returns 400 tokens. On Azure OpenAI, how many tokens does the TPM check reserve for this call (ignore `best_of`)?
quiz.explain: Azure counts prompt plus `max_tokens` up front, so 600 + 4000 = 4,600 [[r9]]. The 400 actual output tokens are irrelevant to the reservation.

quiz.q: A 429 arrives and `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens` is well below the TPM you assigned. Which cause is most likely?
options: A temporary rate-limit adjustment on Standard
quiz.explain: Azure lists a temporary adjustment as one of the documented 429 causes and tells you to compare the limit header with assigned TPM [[r8]]. A malformed body returns 400, and assigned quota is unchanged.

quiz.q: You use Anthropic and set a high `max_tokens` for safety. Which statement is correct?
options: It reserves tokens up front exactly as on Azure
It does not count toward OTPM, which counts actual output
quiz.explain: Anthropic's OTPM counts actual output only, unlike OpenAI and Azure [[r17]]. ITPM concerns input tokens, so a larger output cap does not change it.

flashcards.front: What are Azure's three causes of 429?
flashcards.back: Quota exceeded, system capacity throttling, and a temporary rate-limit adjustment on Standard. Compare the limit header with assigned TPM.
Azure and OpenAI count it toward the limit up front, so each call reserves 4,000 tokens whatever it generates.
429 for the rate limit and 403 for the quota. Counters are per gateway, and streaming always estimates.
